question.text: If the point <math><mi>M</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>,</mo><mi></mi><mi>k</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> lie on the line <math><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math> such that <math><mfenced close="|" open="|" separators="|"><mrow><mi>M</mi><mi>A</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>M</mi><mi>B</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> is maximum where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo></math> then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> is

solution.text:
As, MA-MB≤AB
∴MA-MBmaximum=AB, which is possible when M is the point of intersection of the line joining A1,2, B2,3 and 2x+3y=5.

Equation of the line joining A & B is x-y+1=0

Hence, the point of intersection is h=25, k=75

Hence, h+k=95=1.8
